findings.title: `AssignmentSource.queued` default is captured once at class definition, not per instance
findings.body: The default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the dataclass body is executed (module import time). Every `AssignmentSource` instantiated without explicitly passing `queued` therefore shares the same stale timestamp from import. To get a per-instance timestamp, declare the field with `field(default_factory=lambda: timezone.now())`. The field is unused by current logic, so the bug is latent, but it will surface the moment `queued` is read for ordering, display, or diagnostics.

findings.title: `from_dict` does not validate field types; type coercion can defeat the cycle check
findings.body: `cls(**input_dict)` relies on dataclass `__init__`, which does not enforce the declared type annotations. If `assignment_source_dict` is deserialized by a JSON-based serializer (Celery or otherwise), `integration_id` will arrive as a string and be stored as a string. The downstream comparison `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` then compares a string to an int and is always False in Python, so the cycle-blocking guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` never trips. The `try/except (ValueError, TypeError)` only catches unexpected kwargs / bad dataclass values, not silent type coercion. Validate types (e.g. `isinstance(input_dict.get('integration_id'), int)`) before constructing the dataclass, and reject the input by returning `None` if the cast fails.

findings.title: `test_to_dict` does not verify that `queued` is approximately the current time
findings.body: The test only asserts `result.get('queued') is not None`, which passes even though `queued` is the module-import timestamp (because `timezone.now()` was captured once at class definition). The test should bracket `queued` between two `timezone.now()` calls (e.g. `assert before <= source.queued <= after`) so the latent default-factory bug is caught.

findings.title: Typo in test method name: `inalid` should be `invalid`
findings.body: The method `test_from_dict_inalid_data` has a clear spelling mistake. Rename to `test_from_dict_invalid_data` so the test reads correctly and is discoverable.
